title: BEKOS AND KOUTROPOULOS v. GREECE
summary: In the case of Bekos and Koutroupoulos v. Greece, the applicants, Mr. Lazaros Bekos and Mr. Eleftherios Koutroupoulos, are Greek citizens belonging to the Roma community, represented by the European Roma Rights Center and the Greek Helsinki Monitor. The case highlights the vulnerability of Roma and Travellers to police violence and discrimination, particularly in the context of criminal proceedings. On 8 May 1998, in Mesolonghi, Western Greece, the two young Roma men were arrested by police responding to an attempted burglary. Both applicants alleged that, following their arrest, they were subjected to severe physical abuse and degrading treatment by police officers, including beatings with truncheons, threats of sexual assault, and repeated racist insults referencing their Roma origin. Medical evidence documented significant injuries, and the applicants reported hearing each other’s cries during their detention. Despite their complaints, the investigation by Greek authorities was limited, and only one officer received a minor penalty. The European Court of Human Rights examined the case under Articles 3 (prohibition of torture and inhuman or degrading treatment), 13 (right to an effective remedy), and 14 (prohibition of discrimination) of the Convention. The Court declared the application admissible, recognising the serious issues raised regarding police ill-treatment and possible ethnic discrimination. This case is significant as it reflects the persistent challenges Roma communities face in Europe, particularly regarding police abuse and the lack of effective remedies, against a backdrop of longstanding discrimination.
